messages:
pagerbot: ALERT: SLA breach candidate for tenant=PulseHealth — 99th latency > 1.2s over last 10m (check: tenant-heartbeat-99p). Paging on-call now.

jess (oncall): acked. I'm looking. seeing spike on the 99p from a subset of hosts. grabbing traces.

jess (oncall): quick snapshot: 99p jumped to ~1.35s at 14:12 UTC and stayed high for ~8m, then oscillated.  P50/P90 mostly fine.

anna (sre-lead): thanks. this smells like either a noisy tenant check or a client-side retry amplification. henry, can you pull up recent host CPU/IO for the GPU pool serving embeddings for PulseHealth?

henry (mlops): pulling now. host metrics look normal. no CPU spike, no OOM. network p95 is elevated for a handful of qps from eu-west-1. attaching logs in a sec.

metrics-bot: Attached: timeseries link -> https://metrics.internal.redwood/tenant/PulseHealth/latency?from=1728452100&to=1728456100

jess (oncall): checking alert config: this is the tenant-heartbeat-99p check defined in datadog. current rule: `avg(last_5m):percentile(99, service.response_time{tenant:PulseHealth}) > 1.2` with no sustained window. triggering on short spikes.

jess (oncall): immediate mitigation: proposing a temporary mute for this tenant's pager for 30m while we validate. also add a 10m sustained condition. thoughts?

anna (sre-lead): +1 to temporary mute. we should avoid suppressing real customer-impacting events though. do we have customer-visible errors or only latency?

jess (oncall): only latency — no elevated 5xx, no increase in error-rate for PulseHealth. front-end traces show some requests with slightly longer tail.

sam (product): from product POV, reach out to PulseHealth if we see persistence >30m. but ok to mute pages for 30m while you tune. document action in thread.

henry (mlops): I'll create a tenant-scoped debounce rule and a dashboard panel. Proposed datadog rule update (rolled out as an override for PulseHealth):
```
alert: pulsehealth_99p_sustained
condition: percentile(99, service.response_time{tenant:PulseHealth}).over("10m") > 1.2
notify: oncall
mute_duration: 30m (temp)
```

jess (oncall): executing temporary mute now: `/pager mute tenant:PulseHealth 30m --reason "suspected noisy 99p spikes, tuning in progress"`

pagerbot: pager muted for PulseHealth for 30 minutes by jess (oncall).

anna (sre-lead): while muted, let's create a short dashboard with these panels: 1) per-host 99p latency for PulseHealth, 2) request volume by route, 3) client retry headers, 4) backend queue depth. henry can you spin that up and share link?

henry (mlops): created: https://dash.internal.redwood/tiles/172845-dash-pulsehealth . also added an annotation for mute at 14:18 UTC.

jess (oncall): looking at traces — a small percentage of requests are hitting a fallback model variant which has higher latency. this is probably the cause. we have automatic routing to variant-b when variant-a is saturated.

anna (sre-lead): ok that's actionable. if variant-fallback is causing the 99p tail, we should consider: 1) adjusting the fallback policy to route fewer requests, 2) warm the fallback variant to reduce latency, or 3) raise the threshold for the tenant-specific 99p alert.

sam (product): want to know if users experienced perceived slowdown. no increase in support tickets yet. i'd prefer warming over changing customer-facing routing.

henry (mlops): warming fallback variant now (preload cache, increase upstream replicas). ETA 10m.

jess (oncall): re-checking metrics — after warming started at 14:26 UTC, 99p dropped toward baseline but still noisy for a few minutes.

metrics-bot: note: 99p dropped to 1.05s by 14:35 UTC. sustained window now looks clear.

anna (sre-lead): great. plan: (a) temporarily mute until 14:48 UTC (done), (b) create permanent tenant-specific alert with a sustained window (10m) to reduce chatter, (c) add fallback-variant latency to our per-tenant dashboard, (d) create a runbook entry for PulseHealth fallback behavior. jess, can you file the follow-up?

jess (oncall): filing ticket: RDW-INC-4872 — "PulseHealth: reduce noisy 99p paging, add sustained alert + dashboard + runbook". assigning to eng-runtime (henry) and SRE (anna). link: https://issues.internal.redwood/RDW-INC-4872

jess (oncall): temporary mute expires in 18m. will monitor.

henry (mlops): PR for datadog override created: https://git.internal.redwood/alerts/pulsehealth-sustained-pr — includes rule: `percentile(99, service.response_time{tenant:PulseHealth}).over("10m") > 1.2` and adds a tag `owner:eng-runtime`. request review from anna.

anna (sre-lead): reviewing. also request that eng-runtime adds a metric for `fallback_variant_latency_ms` and emits it per-tenant so we can alert on that specifically instead of the generic 99p.

sam (product): one more ask: could we also add a dashboard panel showing SLA-eligible traffic vs best-effort traffic for PulseHealth? helps triage product vs infra issues.

henry (mlops): will add that. quick config snippet for Datadog mute via CLI if anyone needs it later:
```
dd mute --scope "tenant:PulseHealth" --duration 1800 --comment "temp mute during tuning"
```

jess (oncall): mute expired at 14:48 UTC. no new pages since warming. closing active page. leaving follow-up ticket open for permanent changes.

pagerbot: NOTE: page resolved for tenant=PulseHealth at 14:48 UTC. duration: 30m.

anna (sre-lead): post-incident actions (short):
- eng-runtime to merge datadog override and add `fallback_variant_latency_ms` metric (due EOD).
- eng-platform to add sustained 99p rule to per-tenant templates to prevent immediate churn (due 48h).
- create runbook entry for tenant-specific muting policy and criteria (due 72h).

jess (oncall): adding runbook stub here: "If tenant 99p spikes but no 5xx increase and trace shows fallback variant involvement -> mute page up to 30m, warm fallback, open RDW-INC ticket, do not mute more than twice without customer outreach."

sam (product): thanks folks. i'll flag PulseHealth account manager with a heads-up and include our mitigation steps.

henry (mlops): created follow-up PRs and dashboard updates. linking in RDW-INC-4872.

jess (oncall): closing thread. will ping here if things regress. :thumbsup:
